paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the Most High rules, and He gives the kingdom to whom He wishes (Daniel 4:17). Nebuchadnezzar stood on his palace roof and said, “Is this not Babylon the Great, which I myself have built as a royal residence by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?” (Daniel 4:30). Pride is looking at everything in your life and saying, "I did that," and forgetting WHO handed you the dough in the first place.

Now notice how much mercy is packed into this story. God sent a dream before the sentence, and Daniel urged the king to break away from his sins by doing what is right and showing mercy to the oppressed (Daniel 4:27). Then the stump stayed in the ground, and the kingdom was promised back as soon as the king acknowledged that Heaven rules (Daniel 4:26). I think that's how the Most High works: He humbles, but He leaves a way home.

And look where the king ends up. He looks up to heaven, his sanity is restored, and he praises the King of heaven, saying, “all His works are true and all His ways are just. And He is able to humble those who walk in pride.” (Daniel 4:37). So here's my question for you, baker: what are you tempted to say "I built that" about? Hand it back to Him today, with a thankful heart, and you'll stand a lot steadier than any man on a palace roof.
